#' Update a bslib theme with new Sass variables
#'
#' @description
#' Updates an existing [bs_theme()] by adding or overriding Sass variable
#' declarations. Variables are prepended to the Sass bundle so they take
#' effect during compilation.
#'
#' @param theme A [bs_theme()] object.
#' @param ... Named arguments where names are Sass variable names (without $)
#'   and values are CSS color values or other Sass-compatible values.
#' @return A modified [bs_theme()] object.
#' @export
bs_theme_update <- function(theme, ...) {
  args <- list(...)
  
  sass_vars <- character(0)
  
  for (nm in names(args)) {
    val <- args[[nm]]
    if (!is.null(val)) {
      sass_vars <- c(sass_vars, paste0("$", nm, ": ", val, " !default;"))
    }
  }
  
  # Variables are injected as Sass defaults (!default)
  # This means Bootstrap's own _variables.scss will use these values
  # instead of its built-in defaults.
  #
  # The compilation order is:
  #   1. User-supplied defaults (these variables)
  #   2. Bootstrap _variables.scss (picks up !default values)
  #   3. Bootstrap _root.scss (generates CSS custom properties)
  #   4. Bootstrap component SCSS (uses $vars, NOT custom properties)
  #   5. bslib component overrides
  #
  # IMPORTANT: body-color is consumed by _variables.scss but
  # the generated --bs-body-color custom property in _root.scss
  # is only used by the <body> element in _reboot.scss.
  # Individual components like .card, .modal, .nav-link set
  # their own color from separate Sass variables, NOT from
  # --bs-body-color. This means the brand foreground color
  # won't automatically propagate to all text in the app.
  
  if (length(sass_vars) > 0) {
    sass_bundle <- sass::sass_layer(
      defaults = paste(sass_vars, collapse = "\n")
    )
    theme <- sass::sass_bundle(theme, sass_bundle)
  }
  
  theme
}

#' @rdname bs_theme_update
#' @param body_color The body text color (maps to $body-color)
#' @param body_bg The body background color (maps to $body-bg)
#' @export
bs_theme_colors <- function(theme, body_color = NULL, body_bg = NULL,
                             primary = NULL, secondary = NULL, ...) {
  args <- list(
    `body-color` = body_color,
    `body-bg` = body_bg,
    primary = primary,
    secondary = secondary,
    ...
  )
  args <- Filter(Negate(is.null), args)
  bs_theme_update(theme, !!!args)
}

SUBMIT(answer = "The brand.yml `foreground` color follows this path through bslib's Sass compilation pipeline:

**Path: brand.yml -> Sass -> CSS**
1. `_brand.yml` foreground value is read by `bs_theme_brand()` in `R/bs-theme-brand.R`
2. It maps directly to Bootstrap's `$body-color` Sass variable
3. `$body-color` is injected as a Sass `!default` declaration via `bs_theme_update()`
4. During Sass compilation, `_root.scss` generates `--bs-body-color: #{$body-color}` as a CSS custom property
5. `_reboot.scss` applies `color: var(--bs-body-color)` to the `<body>` element

**The Gap (bslib #1123):**
The foreground color does NOT propagate to all text contexts because:

- Bootstrap components (cards, modals, navbars, nav-links) compile their text colors from **separate Sass variables** (`$card-color`, `$modal-color`, `$nav-link-color`), not from `$body-color`
- These component-level variables default to `null` or their own values, falling back to CSS `inherit` rather than `var(--bs-body-color)`
- bslib's own components (value boxes, cards) sometimes set explicit colors that bypass the cascade entirely
- The CSS custom property `--bs-body-color` exists in `:root` but is only consumed by the `<body>` rule in `_reboot.scss`

In practice, this means setting `foreground: '#1a1a2e'` in brand.yml will color direct body text correctly, but text inside cards, modals, sidebar content, and other component containers may not pick up the brand foreground color. The fix would require bslib to either (a) generate additional CSS custom properties that components reference, or (b) explicitly map `$body-color` to all component-level color variables during theme construction.")

final_answer:
The brand.yml `foreground` color follows this path through bslib's Sass compilation pipeline:

**Path: brand.yml -> Sass -> CSS**
1. `_brand.yml` foreground value is read by `bs_theme_brand()` in `R/bs-theme-brand.R`
2. It maps directly to Bootstrap's `$body-color` Sass variable
3. `$body-color` is injected as a Sass `!default` declaration via `bs_theme_update()`
4. During Sass compilation, `_root.scss` generates `--bs-body-color: #{$body-color}` as a CSS custom property
5. `_reboot.scss` applies `color: var(--bs-body-color)` to the `<body>` element

**The Gap (bslib #1123):**
The foreground color does NOT propagate to all text contexts because:

- Bootstrap components (cards, modals, navbars, nav-links) compile their text colors from **separate Sass variables** (`$card-color`, `$modal-color`, `$nav-link-color`), not from `$body-color`
- These component-level variables default to `null` or their own values, falling back to CSS `inherit` rather than `var(--bs-body-color)`
- bslib's own components (value boxes, cards) sometimes set explicit colors that bypass the cascade entirely
- The CSS custom property `--bs-body-color` exists in `:root` but is only consumed by the `<body>` rule in `_reboot.scss`

In practice, this means setting `foreground: '#1a1a2e'` in brand.yml will color direct body text correctly, but text inside cards, modals, sidebar content, and other component containers may not pick up the brand foreground color. The fix would require bslib to either (a) generate additional CSS custom properties that components reference, or (b) explicitly map `$body-color` to all component-level color variables during theme construction.
